A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across appendix reorganization and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Transformer training experiments, attention interventions, and analyses of Pythia and OLMo checkpoints, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a composite algorithmic task, attention-output probing, additional LLM evaluations, and optimization sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The main Transformer architecture, training objective, decoding procedure, and attention-bias/freezing interventions are retained. The explicit multiplicative mask clarifies the existing intervention. Probing and optimizer variations are additional experiments rather than revisions to the central model.

E1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds a composite task requiring sequential output blocks for copying, two-element sums, and three-element sums. LLM diagnostic coverage expands from ARC-Easy to mathematical GSM8K prompts and ARC-Challenge prompts (Appendix E), substantially broadening the tested input populations while retaining earlier tasks.

E2.justification: Optimizer comparisons expand beyond Adam and SGD to Muon combined with Adam or AdamW, and standalone AdamW experiments. Figure 32 explicitly compares Muon training dynamics with the Adam experiment in Figure 2a. The existing attention-intervention and frozen-component comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include probing every 10 training steps with 1,024 training and 1,024 held-out samples, quantitative LLM repetition measurements, and sweeps over optimizers, learning rates, schedules, initialization scales, batch sizes, weight decay, and L2 regularization. These substantially extend evaluation design; the original main training protocol is retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test sequential partial-solution learning in the composite task, whether attention outputs contain decodable answers before the model succeeds, and sensitivity to numerous optimization choices (Appendices B.7, C, and G). Earlier architecture, softmax-attention, and SGD checks are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 adds no defined confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure. The newly disclosed smoothing in Figure 36 is for presentation, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New findings include staged learning of the composite task, probe accuracy improving before model accuracy, repetition/collapse on additional prompt datasets, and optimization-dependent plateau behavior, including an approximately 40-step plateau with Muon plus Adam. Figure 8 also adds repetition-frequency curves and revises the ARC-Easy cosine traces. Most earlier experimental curves and the reported OLMo values are retained.

T1.justification: The existing Transformer and metric equations are retained. Table 2 makes the existing task-specific APM position sets explicit, and the mask notation restates the previously described intervention. No theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or revised theoretical assumption is introduced; the search explanation remains a hypothesis.

C1.justification: The abstract and five principal contribution statements retain their substantive claims. The Discussion adds token search as a possible explanation for slow attention learning and identifies theoretical validation of this explanation as future work, modestly extending the concluding claims.

C2.justification: Where v1 leaves slow attention learning unexplained, v2 proposes a search phase in which attention gradually identifies relevant input tokens, drawing analogies with earlier learning-dynamics studies. Sections 4 and 8 explicitly distinguish this interpretation from a theoretically validated mechanism.

D1.justification: v2 supplies explicit per-task APM indices, a formal intervention mask, probe architecture and implementation details, and numerical settings for the new optimization studies. It also clarifies integer token IDs, random ARC-Easy sampling, and the fixed embedding width in the head-count experiment. These materially expand reproducibility information; the code link and hardware disclosure already existed.

R1.justification: Sections 4 and 7 substantially expand connections to prior hidden progress, partial solutions, early repetition, attention interventions, attention transfer, and search dynamics. Added works include Abbe et al., Chang et al., Li et al., Panigrahi et al., and Varre et al. The positioning is more explicit about precedents; retained statistical-physics and simplicity-bias discussion moves to Appendix I.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the overall section sequence remain intact. Editing concentrates on Section 4, the rewritten related-work discussion, merged subsection headings, and reorganized appendices separating model configurations from optimization settings. Equation numbering, bibliography style, venue text, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: New displays cover the composite task, probing, additional LLM datasets, and optimization sweeps. Figure 8 gains repetition curves, a second axis, and an expanded caption; Table 1 gains a task and Table 2 documents APM sets. Existing figures are extensively redistributed, including the unchanged random-sampling plot moving from Figure 30 to Figure 25.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the paper's central empirical claims. Held-out probing corroborates hidden progress, optimization tests extend v1's architecture/SGD checks, and quantitative LLM repetition curves replace reliance on qualitative examples while broadening prompt coverage. Explicit APM specifications and clearer acknowledgment of prior findings improve reproducibility and positioning. The search mechanism remains unproved and run-to-run uncertainty remains undocumented, but these limitations do not negate the substantial evidential gains.
